page: Microsoft Azure L16aos_v4 is a storage and memory-optimized server instance powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor. Built on the x86_64 architecture, this instance features 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 8 physical cores with multithreading enabled at 2.0 threads per core. The processor operates at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz and includes 32 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache. It is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, providing a resource density of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Storage is a key component of this instance, which bundles 11,519 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and supports Premium Storage. The instance runs on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor and does not include any GPUs.

Benchmark data reveals strong single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core CPU and Geekbench single-core scores placing in the top 25%. Text processing and text generation for small language models also demonstrate strong performance. However, multi-core CPU performance, Passmark scores, and Redis SET operations fall into the average category. A notable hardware tradeoff is observed in memory bandwidth; while cached small-block read-only bandwidth is average, uncached large-block read-only memory bandwidth is weak, falling into the bottom 25%. Additionally, large-scale LLM inference is highly constrained, with prompt processing for a 70B model rated as poor.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the L16aos_v4 offers high local storage density and a solid memory-to-vCPU ratio, making it a resource-dense option for workloads that require substantial local scratch space or caching without the overhead of external storage arrays. This hardware profile is highly suitable for relational and non-relational databases, large-scale data processing, and local file indexing. It is also well-suited for applications requiring strong single-threaded performance alongside high-capacity local NVMe storage, though it is less optimal for memory-bandwidth-intensive parallel computing or large-scale AI inference.
description: The Microsoft Azure L16aos_v4 is a storage-focused server instance powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor running at 3.7 GHz. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs across 8 physical cores, 128.0 GB of RAM, and a substantial 11,519 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. Operating under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, the instance delivers strong single-core CPU and text processing performance, though its multi-core benchmarks and uncached large-block memory read bandwidth are average to weak. Lacking GPU acceleration, it is not designed for heavy AI workloads, as evidenced by poor large-model LLM inference speeds. However, its high local storage capacity and 8:1 memory-to-core ratio make it qualitatively cost-efficient for database hosting, data warehousing, and I/O-intensive workloads requiring rapid local storage access.
